answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a unique, verifiable hardware-backed identity token, like a quartz-signed attestation from a trusted enclave, before it may trade. Newcomers must forge their reputation slowly through small, observable tasks that peers audit, so a flood of fake identities cannot instantly buy trust. Honest agents earn a beacon score that grows only with sustained useful work and decays when they vanish, making identity farming expensive while real contributors stay visible.
